title: Never oiling the slide and the woman teacher
summary: A woman teacher at the school finds his slide corroded because he never oiled it; he explains why he preferred her to Jackson.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: And he had a lady there that was a teacher, she was a teacher and instructor in the school. So one day I happened to get her to give me my lessons, see. So she taking my horn to show me a passage, you know, how it should be played.
And she got the thing and she couldn't hardly move the slide.

She said, well when have you oiled it last? I said, oiled it last? I said, oiled it last? I said, I've never oiled it. She said, you mean you've never even put it, it was turning green, it was all canker. And then she went on to explain to me that you would have to put oil on the slide.
And how to take care of it.

But he has been not an instrumentalist on this particular instrument. He never told me to find points about the thing, so I didn't know anything about that. So from then on, I mean, I would try to get her every time I could. Because Mr. Jackson, musically, he was terrific. He was, but he was real cruel and real hard. I'll never forget his feet. He must have wore about a twelve or fourteen shoe. And if I would get the pattern of time wrong, which learning music you will, he would just take his feet and stamp right down on me. So I formed an awful dislike for him. An awful dislike for him. But I appreciated him running the rudiments. So I stayed with him for some time. But I would, as I say, I would always try and duck in this anyway possible to give this lady, because she could play the trauma. She could play the trauma. She was a lady, do you remember? I don't remember her name. No, it's been too long.
